<h3 id="failure"><code>Failure</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Failure(self: &TomlParser) -> TomlParseFailure?
```

Why parsing stopped, positioned, or `none` while nothing has gone wrong.
A caller using [`Parse`](/docs/api/toml/toml-parser#parse) never needs this: the failure comes back in the result.

**Returns**: the failure, or `none`

<h3 id="parse"><code>Parse</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Parse(self: &var TomlParser) -> TomlValue ! TomlParseFailure
```

Reads the whole document into a table.
On failure the table holds whatever had been read before the refusal, and `Outcome` says what stopped it
and where. A partial document is not a usable one; it is returned rather than discarded so a caller can
show what was understood before the line that was not.
What comes back is the values and nothing else. Comments never reach the parser, and neither does the
blank line someone put between two sections or the fact that a number was written in hexadecimal. This
reads configuration; it does not edit files.

**Returns**: the document, or the failure and where it was found

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Toml/Src/Parser.rux#L830)
